chapter.li: Verse25 And it came to pass that after Abinadi had made an end of these sayings, that he said unto them, Have 2PP ye taught this people that they should observe to do all these things for to keep these commandments? VerseEnd Verse26 I say unto 2PP you, nay; for if 2PP ye had, the Lord would not have caused me to come forth and to prophesy evil concerning this people. VerseEnd Verse27 And now 2PP ye have said that salvation cometh by the law of Moses. I say unto 2PP you that it is expedient that 2PP ye should keep the law of Moses as yet; but I say unto 2PP you that the time shall come when it shall no more be expedient to keep the law of Moses. VerseEnd Verse28 And moreover, I say unto 2PP you that salvation doth not come by the law alone; and were it not for the atonement which God himself shall make for the sins and iniquities of his people, that they must unavoidably perish, notwithstanding the law of Moses. VerseEnd Verse29 And now I say unto 2PP you that it was expedient that there should be a law given to the children of Israel, yea, even a very strict law. For they were a stiffnecked people, quick to do iniquity and slow to remember the Lord their God. VerseEnd Verse30 Therefore there was a law given them, yea, a law of performances and of ordinances, a law which they were to observe strictly from day to day, to keep them in remembrance of God and their duty towards him. VerseEnd Verse31 But behold, I say unto 2PP you that all these things were types of things to come. VerseEnd

Verse32 And now did they understand the law? I say unto 2PP you, nay, they did not all understand the law — and this because of the hardness of their hearts — for they understood not that there could not any man be saved except it were through the redemption of God. VerseEnd Verse33 For behold, did not Moses prophesy unto them concerning the coming of the Messiah and that God should redeem his people? Yea, and even all the prophets who have prophesied ever since the world began — have they not spoken more or less concerning these things? VerseEnd Verse34 Have they not said that God himself should come down among the children of men, and take upon him the form of man, and go forth in mighty power upon the face of the earth? VerseEnd Verse35 Yea, and have they not said also that he should bring to pass the resurrection of the dead? And that he himself should be oppressed and afflicted? VerseEnd

LEChapter14 Verse1 Yea, even doth not Isaiah say, Who hath believed our report? And to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? VerseEnd Verse2 For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground. He hath no form nor comeliness, and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. VerseEnd Verse3 He is despised and rejected of men — a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief. And we hid, as it were, our faces from him. He was despised and we esteemed him not. VerseEnd Verse4 Surely he hath borne our griefs and carried our sorrows, yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. VerseEnd

Verse5 But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and with his stripes we are healed. VerseEnd Verse6 All we, like sheep, have gone astray — we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquities of us all. VerseEnd Verse7 He was oppressed and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth; he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter; and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he opened not his mouth. VerseEnd Verse8 He was taken from prison and from judgment. And who shall declare his generation? VerseEnd Verse9 For he was cut off out of the land of the living; for the transgressions of my people was he stricken. And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death. Because he had done no evil, neither was any deceit in his mouth; VerseEnd Verse10 yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief.

When 2PSI thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed; he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand. VerseEnd Verse11 He shall see of the travail of his soul and shall be satisfied; by his knowledge shall my righteous Servant justify many, for he shall bear their iniquities. VerseEnd Verse12 Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong — because he hath poured out his soul unto death, and he was numbered with the transgressors, and he bare the sins of many, and made intercession for the transgressors. VerseEnd

LEChapter15 Verse1 And now Abinadi said unto them, I would that 2PP ye should understand that God himself shall come down among the children of men and shall redeem his people. VerseEnd Verse2 And because he dwelleth in flesh, he shall be called the Son of God; and having subjected the flesh to the will of the Father, being the Father and the Son — VerseEnd Verse3 the Father because he was conceived by the power of God, and the Son because of the flesh, thus becoming the Father and Son VerseEnd Verse4 (and they are one God, yea, the very Eternal Father of Heaven and of earth), VerseEnd Verse5 and thus the flesh becoming subject to the spirit, or the Son to the Father, being one God — suffereth temptation and yieldeth not to the temptation, but suffereth himself to be mocked, and scourged, and cast out, and disowned by his people. VerseEnd

Verse6 And after all this, and after working many mighty miracles among the children of men, he shall be led, yea, even as Isaiah said, As a sheep before the shearer is dumb, so he opened not his mouth. VerseEnd Verse7 Yea, even so he shall be led, crucified, and slain, the flesh becoming subject even unto death, the will of the Son being swallowed up in the will of the Father. VerseEnd Verse8 And thus God breaketh the bands of death, having gained the victory over death, giving the Son power to make intercession for the children of men, VerseEnd Verse9 having ascended into Heaven, having the bowels of mercy, being filled with compassion toward the children of men, standing betwixt them and justice, having broken the bands of death, having taken upon himself their iniquity and their transgressions, having redeemed them and satisfied the demands of justice. VerseEnd

Verse10 And now I say unto 2PP you, who shall declare his generation? Behold, I say unto 2PP you that when his soul has been made an offering for sin, he shall see his seed. And now what say 2PP ye? And who shall be his seed? VerseEnd Verse11 Behold, I say unto 2PP you that whosoever has heard the words of the prophets, yea, all the holy prophets who have prophesied concerning the coming of the Lord, I say unto 2PP you that all those who have hearkened unto their words, and believed that the Lord would redeem his people, and have looked forward to that day for a remission of their sins, I say unto 2PP you that these are his seed, or they are heirs of the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse12 For these are they whose sins he hath borne; these are they for whom he has died, to redeem them from their transgressions. And now, are they not his seed? VerseEnd Verse13 Yea, and are not the prophets, every one that has opened his mouth to prophesy that has not fallen into transgression? (I mean all the holy prophets ever since the world began.) I say unto 2PP you that they are his seed. VerseEnd Verse14 And these are they who have published peace, who have brought good tidings of good, who have published salvation and said unto Zion, 2PSI Thy God reigneth. VerseEnd Verse15 And oh how beautiful upon the mountains were their feet. VerseEnd Verse16 And again, how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of those that art still publishing peace. VerseEnd Verse17 And again, how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of those who shall hereafter publish peace, yea, from this time henceforth and for ever! VerseEnd

Verse18 And behold, I say unto 2PP you, this is not all; for oh how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings — that is, the Founder of Peace, yea, even the Lord, who has redeemed his people, yea, him who hath granted salvation unto his people! VerseEnd Verse19 For were it not for the redemption which he hath made for his people, which was prepared from the foundation of the world, I say unto 2PP you, were it not for this, that all mankind must have perished. VerseEnd Verse20 But behold, the bands of death shall be broken, and the Son reigneth and hath power over the dead; therefore he bringeth to pass the resurrection of the dead. VerseEnd Verse21 And there cometh a resurrection, even a first resurrection, yea, even a resurrection of those that have been, and who are, and who shall be, even until the resurrection of Christ — for so shall he be called. VerseEnd Verse22 And now the resurrection of all the prophets and all those that have believed in their words (or all those that have kept the commandments of God) shall come forth in the first resurrection; therefore they are the first resurrection. VerseEnd Verse23 They are raised to dwell with God, who has redeemed them. Thus they have eternal life through Christ, who hath broken the bands of death. VerseEnd

Verse24 And there are those who have part in the first resurrection; and these are they that have died before Christ came, in their ignorance, not having salvation declared unto them. And thus the Lord bringeth about the restoration of these, and they have a part in the first resurrection or have eternal life, being redeemed by the Lord. VerseEnd Verse25 And little children also have eternal life. VerseEnd

Verse26 But behold, and fear, and tremble before God — for 2PP ye ought to tremble — for the Lord redeemeth none such that rebel against him and die in their sins, yea, even all those that have perished in their sins ever since the world began, that have willfully rebelled against God, that have known the commandments of God and would not keep them. These are they that have no part in the first resurrection. VerseEnd Verse27 Therefore, had 2PP ye not ought to tremble? For salvation cometh to none such, for the Lord hath redeemed none such. Yea, neither can the Lord redeem such, for he cannot deny himself; for he cannot deny justice when it hath its claim. VerseEnd

Verse28 And now I say unto 2PP you that the time shall come that the salvation of the Lord shall be declared to every nation, kindred, tongue, and people. VerseEnd Verse29 Yea, Lord, 2PSI thy watchmen shall lift up their voice; with the voice together shall they sing. For they shall see eye to eye when the Lord shall bring again Zion. VerseEnd Verse30 Break forth into joy. Sing together, 2PP ye waste places of Jerusalem. For the Lord hath comforted his people; he hath redeemed Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse31 The Lord hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God. VerseEnd

LEChapter16 Verse1 And now it came to pass that after Abinadi had spoken these words, he stretched forth his hands and said, The time shall come when all shall see the salvation of the Lord, when every nation, kindred, tongue, and people shall see eye to eye and shall confess before God that his judgments are just. VerseEnd Verse2 And then shall the wicked be cast out, and they shall have cause to howl, and weep, and wail, and gnash their teeth; and this because they would not hearken unto the voice of the Lord. Therefore the Lord redeemeth them not. VerseEnd Verse3 For they are carnal and devilish; and the Devil has power over them, yea, even that old serpent that did beguile our first parents, which was the cause of their fall, which was the cause of all mankind’s becoming carnal, sensual, devilish, knowing evil from good, subjecting themselves to the Devil. VerseEnd Verse4 Thus, all mankind were lost. And behold, they would have been endlessly lost were it not that God redeemed his people from their lost and fallen state. VerseEnd Verse5 But remember that he that persists in his own carnal nature, and goes on in the ways of sin and rebellion against God, he remains in his fallen state and the Devil hath all power over him. Therefore, he is as though there was no redemption made, being an enemy to God; and also is the Devil an enemy to God. VerseEnd

Verse6 And now, if Christ had not come into the world, speaking of things to come as though they had already come, there could have been no redemption. VerseEnd Verse7 And if Christ had not risen from the dead, or have broken the bands of death, that the grave should have no victory and that death should have no sting, there could have been no resurrection. VerseEnd Verse8 But there is a resurrection; therefore the grave hath no victory, and the sting of death is swallowed up in Christ. VerseEnd Verse9 He is the light and the life of the world — yea, a light that is endless, that can never be darkened, yea, and also a life which is endless, that there can be no more death. VerseEnd Verse10 Even this mortal shall put on immortality, and this corruption shall put on incorruption, and shall be brought to stand before the bar of God to be judged of him according to their works, whether they be good or whether they be evil: VerseEnd Verse11 if they be good, to the resurrection of endless life and happiness, and if they be evil, to the resurrection of endless damnation, being delivered up to the Devil who hath subjected them, which is damnation, VerseEnd Verse12 having gone according to their own carnal wills and desires, having never called upon the Lord while the arms of mercy were extended towards them. For the arms of mercy were extended towards them and they would not, they being warned of their iniquities, and yet they would not depart from them. And they were commanded to repent, and yet they would not repent. VerseEnd

Verse13 And now had 2PP ye not ought to tremble and repent of 2PP your sins? And remember, only in and through Christ 2PP ye can be saved. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore, if 2PP ye teach the law of Moses, also teach that it is a shadow of those things which are to come. VerseEnd Verse15 Teach them that redemption cometh through Christ the Lord, who is the very Eternal Father. Amen. VerseEnd
